newsitem.title: INDIA: India ready to put oil debt on fiscal deficit - PTI.
newsitem.headline: India ready to put oil debt on fiscal deficit - PTI.

text.p: India's Finance Ministry is dropping resistance to consolidating a $5.3 billion debt to domestic oil companies in the government's fiscal deficit, Press Trust of India said on Monday.

The news agency reported that Finance Ministry sources said the fiscal deficit is unlikely to rise above 5.2 percent of gross domestic product if the oil pool deficit of 190 billion rupees ($5.3 billion) was added to the government's books.
The agency quoted Finance Ministry sources as saying this figure was within manageable limits, although the 1997/98 budget targeted a deficit of 4.5 percent of GDP.

The oil pool deficit tallies money owed to oil companies for selling their products below market prices to support India's subsidy regime. The deficit ballooned late last year when India left its oil prices unchanged while world prices soared.

Consolidating the oil pool deficit in the government's overall debt, and paying for it by issuing "petro-bonds" was one proposal by a committee charged seeking ways to restructure the oil sector's finances. The Finance Ministry had originally opposed this idea, PTI said.
